about.title: Victorville Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Getting hurt on the job in Victorville raises a question most people have never had to think about: is workers' compensation the whole story, or is there more to it? Under California law, comp is usually the only claim you can bring against your employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. It does not cover pain and suffering, though. That is where a third party comes in. If a subcontractor, a property owner, a defective machine, or another driver played a role in what happened, a separate injury claim may be possible alongside comp. Driving is part of many jobs in San Bernardino County, and Victorville's public crash records reflect that reality: 522 injury collisions and 753 people hurt in 2025, with volume concentrated on Bear Valley Road, Amargosa Road, Mojave Drive, and Rt 395, and a Friday peak between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were behind the wheel for work when a crash happened, both paths may apply. We can help you understand which options apply to you.

items.title: We look past the comp claim
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or driver can be held separately responsible. We know to ask that question early.

items.title: We help you protect your job and your timeline
items.desc: California gives you 30 days to report an injury to your employer, and it is illegal for them to retaliate when you do. Third-party claims carry their own two-year deadline, so getting oriented quickly matters.

items.title: Free consultation, and no fee unless you recover
items.desc: We do not charge you for a case review. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: I was hit on Bear Valley Road while driving for work. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and a portion of lost wages no matter who caused the collision. If the other driver was negligent, you may also have a separate third-party injury claim against that driver for losses comp does not pay, such as pain and suffering. We can help you pursue both without one undermining the other.

items.question: Can my employer punish me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against a worker for reporting an on-the-job injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. You still need to report the injury to your employer within 30 days, so do not delay out of worry. If you experience pushback after reporting, that is worth mentioning when you contact us.

items.question: How long do I have to file a third-party claim in San Bernardino County?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of injury. That clock runs separately from your workers' compensation case, and it does not pause while comp benefits are being sorted out. Getting in touch with us early gives you room to gather evidence and identify every responsible party.
